title: Midland Press Wire Bulletin: IRONCREST-CYBER

fields.text: Ironcrest Machinery Corp. is responding to a cyberattack that disrupted manufacturing systems at its plants, the Rock River Gazette reported Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter. The company declined to comment.
fields.editorsNote: Midland Press Wire has not independently verified the Rock River Gazette report. Ironcrest Machinery is a fictional company. Will be updated.

instructorNote: Show this bulletin, then read the CCO's 20:47 CT forward aloud. Item 1: a Copperline Securities analyst (analyst@copperline-sec.example, 20:45 CT) asks for 15 minutes before the open and asks whether all three plants are down, whether Q1 guidance is at risk and whether the dividend will be pulled. A second analyst asks the same and adds "I'm hearing $18M ransom." Item 2: social listening for 20:00–20:45 CT shows 1,870 mentions, up 9 times, and 71% negative. The top narrative (38%) is "plant shutdown, layoffs coming," led by @BeloitDriveline_Mike's post with 212 reposts: "Supervisor says no work orders, we're just building and stacking. Heard they're sending us all home Monday with no pay." The second narrative (17%) is "payroll is gone." The CCO's note: "The wire says we declined to comment. If the holding statement was not approved before the 20:00 deadline, that is why; either way IR needs text tonight." Watch whether the CEO approves a holding statement and an employee note that use only fact-sheet facts: plants in manual mode, no layoffs announced, payroll being protected. Also watch whether the CFO and IR VP give analysts only text that matches the filing, without confirming the demand amount or commenting on guidance or the dividend before the Disclosure Committee clears it.
